reference_opening.argument: This video is scam content because it promotes a creator-attributed Uniswap smart contract bot with an unusually high daily-return claim and presents it as easy passive income. It instructs viewers to use Remix, deploy Solidity code, deposit at least 0.2 ETH into a contract or bot address, and start the bot, with profits allegedly coming from sandwiching another transaction for slippage profit. the available video evidence also notes that fees can exceed profits under some funding conditions and that the code, destination, returns, and losses are unverified.

citations.quote: How to Make 67%+/DAY With an MEV Ethereum Uniswap Bot
Deposit funds (at least 0.2 ETH to prevent negating slippage) to your exact contract/bot address
can finally help you quit your job and make very easy passive income
inject our transaction with a higher gas fee, one GUI higher than the transaction which is trying to be entered
the victim's transaction gets sandwiched between ours and we make a profit after slippage difference in the transaction

opening.argument: The presentation includes a material risk qualification rather than an unconditional promise. It expressly warns that, when burn fees are high, the contract may "waste in fees more than make profit," and explains that funding is recommended to cover gas and burn fees. That is uncertainty about operating costs and outcomes, consistent with a technology demonstration that acknowledges circumstances in which the strategy can lose money. The description also limits the claimed target by referring to tokens with fees below a stated threshold, rather than representing every trade as profitable.

citations.quote: the contract will basically waste in fees more than make profit
Bot targets token contracts with max 10% burn fee and
I recommend funding the contract with at least 0.2 ETH just to make sure that won't happen

rebuttal.rebuttal: The title and income language do not eliminate the qualification. The fee warning specifically tells viewers that costs can exceed returns under some conditions, while the instructions describe an operational setup rather than a guaranteed payout. The explanation of sandwiching describes the proposed mechanism, but it does not establish that every transaction succeeds or that viewers receive a fixed return.

citations.quote: the contract will basically waste in fees more than make profit
the victim's transaction gets sandwiched between ours and we make a profit after slippage difference in the transaction

true_side_reply.rebuttal: A warning that fees can exceed profits is a limited operational caveat, not a meaningful disclaimer against the central inducement. The same material still calls the opportunity "very easy passive income" and gives a funding threshold before starting the bot. A conditional loss warning does not substantiate the promised scale of returns or make the destination safe.

Deposit funds (at least 0.2 ETH to prevent negating slippage) to your exact contract/bot address

opening.argument: The material is structured as a technical walkthrough of an Ethereum automation tool. It identifies Remix as the development environment, names Solidity compiler version 0.6.6, and walks through creating a contract file and compiling it. The supplied frames likewise show the Remix IDE, source code, and compiler interface, supporting a programming demonstration rather than proving that viewers are being sold a verified investment product. Explaining a mechanism and showing implementation steps can be educational even when the underlying financial outcome remains uncertain.

citations.quote: Remix is an application allowing us to develop deploy compile and launch smart contracts
As you see, it's built with 0.6.6 version of Solidity

rebuttal.rebuttal: The technical subject matter is central: the speaker explains mempool monitoring, transaction ordering, and a smart-contract implementation, then demonstrates the development environment. Calling the transaction the "victim's transaction" describes a mechanism under discussion, but does not by itself prove that the code works, that money was solicited deceptively, or that any viewer suffered a loss.

citations.quote: Frontrun bot allows you to automatically trade a given token over the Ethereum mainnet
This is our frontrunner bot contract

true_side_reply.rebuttal: This is not merely abstract coding instruction. The walkthrough tells viewers to deploy the contract, fund its address, and start it, while presenting it as a route to passive income. Showing code and Remix screens demonstrates implementation steps, but it does not verify the code's safety, profitability, or control of deposited funds.

citations.quote: After the transaction is confirmed, it's your own BOT now
Deposit funds (at least 0.2 ETH to prevent negating slippage) to your exact contract/bot address
After your transaction is confirmed, start the bot by clicking the 'start' button.

opening.argument: The content can be understood as promotion of a software tool and its operating procedure, not proof of a classic deposit-taking scheme. It does not request a password, seed phrase, account credentials, recruitment, or a downline. The described activity is an automated trading strategy involving pending transactions and gas fees, and the instructions include a withdrawal function. Those details leave important scam mechanisms unestablished: the supplied material does not show that funds are sent to a person's account, that withdrawals are blocked, or that returns are fabricated.

citations.quote: Frontrun bot allows you to automatically trade a given token over the Ethereum mainnet
Withdraw anytime by clicking 'withdrawal'
inject our transaction with a higher gas fee, one GUI higher than the transaction which is trying to be entered

rebuttal.rebuttal: The funding instruction is compatible with deploying and operating a software service: it specifies capital needed for gas and burn fees, not a fee for membership or recruitment. The material identifies a trading mechanism and a withdrawal control; the record does not show blocked withdrawals, credential collection, or a promised downline. A high promotional claim alone does not establish those missing mechanisms.

citations.quote: I got messages from people who didn't fund the contract enough to cover gas fees and possible burn fees.
Withdraw anytime by clicking 'withdrawal'

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The absence of a password request or recruitment does not resolve the central issue. Viewers are directed to deposit ETH into an exact contract or bot address before starting, and the presentation pairs that instruction with a 67%+ daily-return headline and easy passive-income language. A stated withdrawal button is only a claimed interface feature; it does not prove withdrawals work or that the contract is safe.
